articles.title: Testing Agent Skills Systematically with Evals
articles.read_scope: Complete main article, sections 1–8, including sample skill, runner, rubric and limitations of lightweight checks; code inspected but not executed.

practice.trigger: A skill or workflow changes and improvement needs evidence.
practice.failure: Activation regressions, skipped actions or stray artifacts hide behind a plausible final answer.
practice.mechanism: Define outcomes first; capture traces and artifacts; combine deterministic checks with independent rubric grading.
practice.conditions: Use isolated repeatable fixtures and explicit, implicit and adjacent nontrigger prompts.
practice.counterexample: Command presence alone can pass after a failed command; inspect exit status and resulting behavior.
practice.verification: Retain prompt, candidate version, environment, trace, artifact diff and per-criterion score.

articles.limitations: Demonstration scaffold, not production benchmark evidence. Verify CLI event shape and flags against the installed version.

articles.title: How we built our multi-agent research system
articles.read_scope: Complete main article and appendix, including evaluation, deployment, recovery and filesystem handoffs.

practice.trigger: A valuable task contains independently investigable subproblems.
practice.failure: Vague delegation duplicates work, misses boundaries or spends excessive effort.
practice.mechanism: Assign scoped objectives, outputs and tool guidance; return evidence-bearing artifacts; checkpoint resumable work.
practice.conditions: Parallelize separable work and scale effort to task complexity.
practice.counterexample: Tightly coupled edits sharing changing state can cost more coordination than they save.
practice.verification: Check final state, intermediate acceptance checkpoints, sources and observed coordination behavior.

articles.limitations: Reported gains are internal research results, not guarantees for coding workflows or today's models. Durable recovery still requires effect identity and runtime enforcement.

articles.title: Context Engineering
articles.read_scope: Complete main article: writing, selecting, compressing and isolating context, plus LangGraph/LangSmith implementation discussion.

practice.trigger: Tool output or repeated handoffs crowd a long-running task.
practice.failure: Relevant decisions disappear among stale, conflicting or irrelevant context.
practice.mechanism: Persist task state externally, retrieve the needed subset, compress completed phases and isolate independent investigations.
practice.conditions: Keep source references and task-critical decisions available after summarization.
practice.counterexample: A smaller summary is harmful if it loses an invariant, unresolved failure or user constraint.
practice.verification: Replay a resumed task and compare retained decisions, outcome, token use and missed evidence.

articles.limitations: Broad synthesis with vendor-specific examples; cited cross-company results are not independent LangChain experiments. Context isolation is not authorization isolation.

articles.title: We removed 80% of our agent’s tools
articles.read_scope: Complete main article including old/new tool snippets, five-query comparison, prerequisites and conclusions; snippets not executed.

practice.trigger: An agent's overlapping tools require repeated routing patches.
practice.failure: Special-purpose wrappers obscure usable context and add decision overhead.
practice.mechanism: Experiment with a smaller tool surface and direct access to well-documented task data.
practice.conditions: The example relied on structured semantic files and sandboxed exploration.
practice.counterexample: Undocumented joins or unsafe write authority are not fixed by exposing a shell.
practice.verification: Compare identical representative tasks for correctness, steps, latency, tokens and invalid effects.

articles.limitations: Only five queries; no universal reliability claim. Despite the introduction's single-tool wording, the shown v2 retains ExecuteSQL beside ExecuteCommand.
